knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum and Constant Factor Rules

question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x^{8}-6}{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(2 x^{6} - \frac{6}{x^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=2\int x^{6}\,\mathrm{d}x-6\int x^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=2\left(\frac{x^{7}}{7}\right)-6\left(\frac{x^{-1}}{-1}\right)+C \\ &=\frac{2x^{7}}{7}+\frac{6}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
